title: What is one of your earliest memories?
text: Where were you? Who was there? What do you see when you picture it?

title: What did the home you grew up in look like?
text: The rooms, the kitchen, the view from a window, the sounds and smells.

title: What games did you play as a child?
text: Who did you play with, and where? Were there any rules only your friends knew?

title: What did the grown-ups in your home do for work?
text: What did you understand about their work as a child?

title: What was a typical Sunday like when you were young?
text: Was it a day for church, visits, a big meal, chores, or something else?

title: What was your neighbourhood like?
text: The shops, the street, the neighbours you remember.

title: Did you have a favourite toy or treasure?
text: Where did it come from, and what happened to it?

title: Do you remember a time you got into trouble as a child?
text: What happened, and how did the grown-ups react?

title: What was your favourite holiday or celebration as a child?
text: What did you eat, wear or do that made it special?

title: Were there any animals in your childhood?
text: A pet, a farm animal, a neighbour’s dog — any creature you remember.

title: What do you remember about the older generation in your family?
text: Grandparents, great-aunts or other elders: how they spoke, what they cooked, what they taught you.

title: What did your family listen to or watch together?
text: A radio programme, a television show, records on Sunday afternoons.

title: Who was a teacher you remember?
text: What made them stand out, for better or worse?

title: Which subjects did you enjoy, and which did you dread?
text: Was there something you were especially good at?

title: What did you dream of becoming when you were young?
text: Where did that dream come from, and what became of it?

title: Who were your closest friends growing up?
text: What did you do together? Are you still in touch?

title: What was a school day like when you were young?
text: How did you get there? What did you eat at lunch? What did you wear?

title: Do you remember your first day at a new school?
text: How did you feel walking in?

title: What happened when you finished school?
text: What choices did you face, and who helped you decide?

title: What music did you love as a teenager?
text: Where did you hear it — the radio, a dance, a friend’s records?

title: What do you remember about your very first job?
text: Where did you work? What did you earn? What was your first day like?

title: Do you remember your first car, bicycle or way of getting around?
text: What did it look like, and where did it take you?

title: When did you first live away from your family home?
text: What was the place like? What did you have to learn quickly?

title: What was your first big adventure?
text: Somewhere you went, something you tried, a risk you took.

title: What did you spend your first wages on?
text: Something sensible, something fun, or something for someone else?

title: Have you ever moved to a new town or country?
text: What did you bring with you? What surprised you when you arrived?

title: What did you wear when you were young and wanted to look your best?
text: A favourite outfit, a hairstyle, something your parents didn’t approve of.

title: Where did young people go to have fun in your day?
text: Dances, cafés, the cinema, the park — what was a good night out?

title: Who has had the greatest influence on your life?
text: What did they say or do that stayed with you?

title: How did you meet someone who became important to you?
text: A friend, a partner, a mentor — where and how did your paths cross?

title: Which friendship has stayed with you the longest?
text: How did it begin, and what has kept it going?

title: What traditions have you shared with the people you love?
text: A recipe, a song, a yearly trip, a saying.

title: Do you remember a kindness someone showed you that you never forgot?
text: What happened, and why did it matter so much?

title: Who were the people in your family as you grew up?
text: Brothers, sisters, cousins, or the people who were family to you.

title: What is the best advice anyone ever gave you?
text: Who gave it, and did you take it?

title: How did you come to do the work you did?
text: Was it a plan, a chance, a family tradition, or something else?

title: What are you most proud of from your working life?
text: It doesn’t have to be paid work: running a home or caring for others counts.

title: What was a challenge you faced at work?
text: How did you get through it?

title: What advice would you give someone starting out in your line of work?
text: What do you wish someone had told you?

title: Who was a memorable person you worked with?
text: What were they like, and what did you learn from them?

title: What did an ordinary working day look like for you?
text: From the time you woke up to the time you got home.

title: How did your kind of work change over the years?
text: New machines, new rules, new ways of doing things.

title: How did you feel when a big chapter of work came to an end?
text: What did you do with your time after?

title: What is the most memorable place you have been?
text: What did you see, hear and eat there?

title: Have you ever lived somewhere unexpected?
text: How did you end up there?

title: What was a favourite holiday or day trip?
text: Where did you go, and how did you get there?

title: Tell me about a journey that didn’t go to plan.
text: A missed train, a wrong turn, an unexpected stop.

title: Is there a place you still think about going back to?
text: What draws you back there?

title: Which big events in the world do you remember living through?
text: Where were you when you heard the news? How did the people around you react?

title: How has technology changed during your lifetime?
text: The first telephone, television or computer you remember using.

title: Do you remember the first television you saw?
text: Whose was it, and what was on?

title: What music takes you straight back to a particular time?
text: Where were you, and who were you with?

title: What change in the world has surprised you most?
text: Something you never expected to see.

title: What did things cost when you were young?
text: A loaf of bread, a bus ticket, a cinema seat, a stamp.

title: What was the first computer, phone or gadget you owned?
text: How did you learn to use it?

title: How did your family get the news when you were growing up?
text: A newspaper, the radio, the neighbours?

title: What accomplishment are you most proud of?
text: Big or small, public or private.

title: What was one of the biggest decisions you ever made?
text: What made you choose the way you did?

title: What challenge taught you something important?
text: What do you understand now that you didn’t before?

title: What is something you taught yourself to do?
text: How did you learn it, and do you still do it?

title: When have you surprised yourself with your own courage?
text: What happened?

title: Was there a moment when your life changed direction?
text: What happened just before, and just after?

title: What meal reminds you of home?
text: Who made it, and when was it served?

title: Is there a recipe you know by heart?
text: Where did you learn it? Talk us through it.

title: What traditions did your family have?
text: For birthdays, holidays, or ordinary evenings.

title: What hobbies have brought you the most joy?
text: How did you get started?

title: What does an ideal day look like for you now?
text: From morning until evening.

title: What does your morning look like these days?
text: Is there a little ritual you enjoy?

title: Is there a place where you feel most at home?
text: A garden, a chair, a café, a walk.

title: Is there an object you own that has a story behind it?
text: Where did it come from, and why do you keep it?

title: Is there a photograph that means a lot to you?
text: Who is in it, and what was happening that day?

title: Is there a song you always sing or hum?
text: Where did you learn it?

title: What advice would you give your younger self?
text: What would you want them to know?

title: What have you learned about friendship?
text: What makes a friend a good one?

title: What does happiness mean to you?
text: Has your answer changed over the years?

title: What do you hope future generations remember?
text: About you, your family, or the times you lived through.

title: What are you grateful for today?
text: Something big, or something very small.

title: What is a mistake you learned from?
text: What would you do differently?

title: What matters most to you, and why?
text: Where did those values come from?

title: What do you wish for the people who come after you?
text: Your family, your community, the world.

title: What is something that always makes you laugh?
text: A story you love telling, a person, a memory.

title: What is something you changed your mind about?
text: What made you see it differently?
